Fix: Apply an advanced audit policy to all DCs by GPO (Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Advanced Audit Policy Configuration), based on the Microsoft or ANSSI recommended settings. Check that the GPO really applies to every DC, including DCs moved out of the 'Domain Controllers' OU.
GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows PowerShell. Enable 'Turn on Module Logging' (module names: *) and 'Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging'.

Back up the system state of at least one DC per domain on a regular schedule, with a tool that does a real AD backup (this updates the backup date PingCastle reads). Example: wbadmin start systemstatebackup -backuptarget:E: . Test a restore from time to time.

A DC still offers SSL 2.0 or SSL 3.0 on LDAPS (port 636). On each DC, create the SCHANNEL keys 'SSL 2.0\Server' and 'SSL 3.0\Server' with Enabled = 0 and DisabledByDefault = 1, then reboot the DC (in the check, an empty value means the Windows default). Plan to turn off TLS 1.0 and 1.1 too, after testing old clients.

Reset the krbtgt password twice. Wait at least 10 hours between the two resets (the default max ticket lifetime; wait longer if you raised it) and make sure replication is done. Microsoft's New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1 script helps you do each reset safely. PingCastle alerts after 1 year, so plan it at least once a year.
Check: Get-ADUser krbtgt -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select-Object Name, PasswordLastSet

Fix: Deploy Windows LAPS (built into Windows since the April 2023 updates; legacy Microsoft LAPS is deprecated): run Update-LapsADSchema, give computers the right to write their password (Set-LapsADComputerSelfPermission on each OU), then turn on the LAPS policy by GPO.

A GPO sets 'Network security: LDAP client signing requirements' to None. Edit that GPO (Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options) and set it to 'Negotiate signing' (the default) or 'Require signing', or remove the setting. Also make DCs require signing; new Windows Server 2025 forests do it by default.

A GPO sets 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' to 'Send LM & NTLM responses' or disables 'Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change'. Edit that GPO: enable 'Do not store LAN Manager hash...' and set the level to at least 'Send NTLMv2 response only', ideally 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM' after checking NTLM audit logs.

A password policy (GPO or fine grained policy) allows passwords shorter than 8 characters. Raise the minimum to at least 12 (PingCastle only needs 8). The domain GPO can't go above 14; use a fine grained policy for longer. Users get the new rule at their next password change.
Check: Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy | Select-Object MinPasswordLength; Get-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Filter * | Select-Object Name, MinPasswordLength, AppliesTo

Fix: Run the NetCease script on a reference server, then push its registry value (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\DefaultSecurity\SrvsvcSessionInfo) to servers and DCs with a GPO Registry preference (Registry Wizard). Restart the Server service or reboot to apply.

Move service accounts to gMSA (or dMSA on Windows Server 2025) so their passwords rotate by themselves. For the others, create a fine grained password policy with a minimum length of 20+ and apply it to a service accounts group.

A DC answers requests without any account. Fix the causes listed by the other rules of the report (A-PreWin2000Anonymous, A-DsHeuristicsAnonymous). On DCs, keep 'Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users' Disabled and 'Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts' Enabled. Then rerun PingCastle to confirm.
Remove 'Everyone' and 'Anonymous Logon' from the 'Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access' group, but keep 'Authenticated Users' in it. Then reboot each DC: the change only applies after a restart.
Remove the extra members added to the 'Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access' group and keep only 'Authenticated Users' (its default). Then reboot each DC.

Move the PDC emulator role to a Windows Server 2012 R2 or newer DC: the 'Protected Users' group is then created and replicated. Then add admin accounts to it after a test. Never add service or computer accounts: they will fail to authenticate.

Treat the passwords found as known by attackers: change them now on every system that uses them. Then delete the Group Policy Preferences items that store them (cpassword in SYSVOL). For local admin passwords, use Windows LAPS instead.

A SHA-1 signed intermediate CA certificate is pushed by a GPO (Public Key Policies) or stored in NTAuth; the report gives the source. Remove it there. If it is still in use, issue a new SHA-256 CA certificate first and reissue the certificates that depend on it.
Check: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\CA | Where-Object { $_.SignatureAlgorithm.FriendlyName -eq 'sha1RSA' } | Select-Object Subject, Thumbprint, NotAfter; certutil -viewstore -enterprise NTAuth

Fix: A SHA-1 signed root certificate is pushed by a GPO (Public Key Policies) or stored in NTAuth; the report gives the source. Remove it there. If it is still in use, replace the CA with a SHA-256 one first and reissue the certificates that depend on it.
Check: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where-Object { $_.Subject -eq $_.Issuer -and $_.SignatureAlgorithm.FriendlyName -eq 'sha1RSA' } | Select-Object Subject, Thumbprint, NotAfter

Fix: Turn on automatic hash rolling: at domain functional level 2016 or higher, set msDS-ExpirePasswordsOnSmartCardOnlyAccounts to True on the domain object, and don't disable the GPO 'Enable rolling of expiring NTLM secrets during sign on...'. Quick one-off fix: untick, then tick again 'Smart card is required for interactive logon' on each account.
Check: Get-ADObject (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName -Properties msDS-ExpirePasswordsOnSmartCardOnlyAccounts | Select-Object msDS-ExpirePasswordsOnSmartCardOnlyAccounts; Get-ADUser -Filter {SmartcardLogonRequired -eq $true} -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select-Object SamAccountName, PasswordLastSet

Fix: Clear the userPassword and unixUserPassword attributes on the listed accounts (Set-ADUser <name> -Clear userPassword, unixUserPassword), unless a system really needs them. Then change those users' passwords, as any user may have read them.

A certificate pushed by a GPO or stored in NTAuth has an RSA key between 1024 and 2048 bits, or under 3072 bits while valid after 2030. Remove it there. If it is still in use, issue a new CA certificate with a longer key (3072+ for long life) and reissue what depends on it.
Check: Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\Root, Cert:\LocalMachine\CA | Where-Object { $_.PublicKey.Oid.FriendlyName -eq 'RSA' -and ($_.PublicKey.Key.KeySize -lt 2048 -or ($_.PublicKey.Key.KeySize -lt 3072 -and $_.NotAfter -gt [datetime]'2031-01-01')) } | Select-Object Subject, NotAfter

Fix: Enabled members of admin groups have a password older than 3 years. Change their passwords now, and disable or delete admin accounts nobody uses. Use long passphrases or smart cards for admins.
Check: $s = (Get-ADDomain).DomainSID; 'S-1-5-32-544', "$s-512", "$s-518", "$s-519" | ForEach-Object { Get-ADGroupMember -Identity $_ -Recursive -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } | Where-Object objectClass -eq 'user' | Get-ADUser -Properties PasswordLastSet | Where-Object { $_.Enabled -and $_.PasswordLastSet -lt (Get-Date).AddYears(-3) } | Sort-Object SamAccountName -Unique | Select-Object SamAccountName, PasswordLastSet

Fix: In the PingCastle HTML report, open the control path chart of this rule: it shows which object (OU, group, GPO, user...) lets everyone-like groups (Everyone, Authenticated Users, Domain Users...) take control of a key object. Remove that write permission, or replace it with a delegation to a dedicated admin group.

Install the October 2021 update (CVE-2021-40469) on all DNS servers; PingCastle made this rule informative after it. Then empty DnsAdmins anyway and give DNS rights per zone to a dedicated group instead.

The report lists the GPO files or folders. Open their permissions (GPMC > the GPO > Delegation, or the folder in SYSVOL) and remove any write right given to Everyone, Authenticated Users, Domain Users or Users. They should only keep Read (and 'Apply group policy' on the GPO).

For each admin account with an SPN: if it is a person, remove the SPN. If it is a service account, take it out of the admin groups and give it only the rights it needs, or move it to a gMSA. If that's not possible, set a long random password (25+ characters) and change it regularly. PingCastle ignores accounts whose password changed in the last 40 days.
Check: Get-ADUser -Filter {ServicePrincipalName -like '*' -and AdminCount -eq 1} -Properties ServicePrincipalName, PasswordLastSet | Select-Object SamAccountName, PasswordLastSet, ServicePrincipalName

Fix: Empty Account Operators, Server Operators, Print Operators and Backup Operators. Put real admins in the right admin group, and give other people only delegated rights on the OUs they manage. Check first what each member really uses (backups, printers...).
Check: 'S-1-5-32-548', 'S-1-5-32-549', 'S-1-5-32-550', 'S-1-5-32-551' | ForEach-Object { $g = Get-ADGroup -Identity $_; Get-ADGroupMember -Identity $_ | Select-Object @{n = 'Group'; e = { $g.Name } }, Name }

Fix: Empty the 'Allowed RODC Password Replication Group'. If some passwords must be cached on an RODC, add a dedicated group to that RODC's own Password Replication Policy instead.

Put back the members PingCastle expects in the 'Denied RODC Password Replication Group': Domain Controllers, Read-only Domain Controllers, Domain Admins, Group Policy Creator Owners, Cert Publishers and krbtgt, plus Enterprise Admins and Schema Admins in the forest root domain.
Remove all members of Schema Admins. Add an account only for a planned schema update, then remove it right after.

Turn off unconstrained delegation on every account that isn't a DC: Set-ADComputer <name> -TrustedForDelegation $false (Set-ADUser for users). If an app needs delegation, use 'Trust this computer for delegation to specified services only' with 'Use Kerberos only'. Also mark admins 'Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated' or put them in Protected Users.
Check: Get-ADComputer -Filter {TrustedForDelegation -eq $true -and PrimaryGroupID -ne 516} | Select-Object Name; Get-ADUser -Filter {TrustedForDelegation -eq $true} | Select-Object SamAccountName

Fix: Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 on the domain (Set-ADDomain (Get-ADDomain) -Replace @{'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota' = 0}). Then let only a dedicated group join computers, with a delegation on the target OU.

Set the primary group of the listed computers back to 'Domain Computers' (515): ADUC > the computer > Member Of > Set Primary Group. DCs use 516 (521 for RODCs). This rule also triggers when a DC is outside the 'Domain Controllers' OU: move it back there.
Check: Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties PrimaryGroupID | Where-Object { $_.PrimaryGroupID -notin 514, 515, 516, 521 } | Select-Object Name, PrimaryGroupID; Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | Where-Object { $_.ComputerObjectDN -notlike "*,$((Get-ADDomain).DomainControllersContainer)" } | Select-Object Name

Fix: Add new DCs on a supported Windows Server (2022 or 2025), move the FSMO roles, then demote and remove the 2008 DC. Don't pick Windows Server 2016 as the target: its support ends on January 12, 2027.

A DC hasn't logged on for 45+ days. If it still runs, fix it or demote it properly. If it is dead, delete its computer account from the 'Domain Controllers' OU in ADUC (this runs the metadata cleanup), then remove its leftover DNS records.
Check: Get-ADDomainController -Filter * | ForEach-Object { Get-ADComputer $_.ComputerObjectDN -Properties LastLogonDate } | Select-Object Name, LastLogonDate

Fix: If no SID History migration is running, delete the '<DOMAIN>$$$' group. If a migration is running, finish it first.
On each listed admin account: Account tab > untick 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication', or run Set-ADAccountControl <name> -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false. This blocks AS-REP roasting.
Upgrade or replace the Windows Server 2008 / 2008 R2 servers with a supported version (2022 or 2025). Until then, isolate them on the network.
Check: Get-ADComputer -Filter {Enabled -eq $true -and OperatingSystem -like '*Server 2008*'} -Properties OperatingSystem | Select-Object Name, OperatingSystem

Fix: Replace or upgrade the Windows 7 machines to Windows 11 (Windows 10 support also ended on October 14, 2025, except with paid ESU). Until then, isolate them on the network.
Check: Get-ADComputer -Filter {Enabled -eq $true -and OperatingSystem -like '*Windows 7*'} -Properties OperatingSystem | Select-Object Name, OperatingSystem

Fix: Untick 'Password never expires' on these accounts and change their passwords. Move service accounts to gMSA. For domain-joined Linux machines, turn on automatic machine password renewal. PingCastle ignores accounts whose password changed in the last 30 days.
Check: Get-ADUser -Filter {PasswordNeverExpires -eq $true -and Enabled -eq $true} -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select-Object SamAccountName, PasswordLastSet

Fix: First update the permissions (shares, file ACLs, apps) that still use the old SIDs so they point to the new accounts. Then clear SID History on users, groups and computers. Once removed, it can't be added back.

Disable SMBv1 on the DCs: Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false, then remove the feature (Uninstall-WindowsFeature FS-SMB1). First check that nothing still uses it (old printers, scanners, old OS): Set-SmbServerConfiguration -AuditSmb1Access $true and watch the SMBServer/Audit event log.

Check if the remote domain still exists and can be reached. If it is gone, delete the trust (Active Directory Domains and Trusts). If it still exists, fix the network or DNS so the trust password rotates again.

For an external (domain) trust: netdom trust <YourDomain> /domain:<OtherDomain> /quarantine:yes. For a forest trust: netdom trust <YourForest> /domain:<OtherForest> /enablesidhistory:no. Never use /quarantine on a forest trust (it breaks transitivity). Finish any running migration first.
Check: Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select-Object Name, Direction, ForestTransitive, SIDFilteringQuarantined, SIDFilteringForestAware
